source: CCwiki derivation curation, 2026-10: what relations.json would need to record for CCwiki to drop its reviewed corrections (axhoover/ccwiki, plans/wiki-asks.md)

items.summary: An equivalence records one class for two directions that can be different theorems; add a required reverse-class (the class of conclusion ⇒ hypothesis) to every equivalence
items.proposed_action: (1) scripts/generate-relations.mjs, in the reductions.push record after `class`: `...(p.fm.kind === "equivalence" ? { reverseClass: p.fm["reverse-class"] ?? "unstated" } : {})`. (2) Lint: add "reverse-class" to OPTIONAL_KEYS (scripts/lint.mjs) and EDGE_FRONTMATTER (scripts/lint-edges.mjs); error `edge-reverse-class-missing` on a `kind: equivalence` page without it and `edge-reverse-class` on any other kind; its value is a class or `unstated`; set RATIONALE_FIELDS.reduction["reverse-class"] = "reverseClass"; the contradiction check reads reverse-class for a barrier on the reverse pair. (3) Docs: docs/relations-json.md § reductions, and schema/README.md § What the hyperedge asserts. (4) Values (class / reverse-class): cpa-security-to-cpa-security fully-black-box / fully-black-box; linear-secret-sharing-schemes-lsss-to-msp free / free; module-lwe-to-lwe-ls15 fully-black-box / fully-black-box; module-lwe-to-ring-lwe-ls15 fully-black-box / fully-black-box; rabin-ot-to-ot fully-black-box / fully-black-box; qip-to-pspace free / free; isis-inhomogeneous-sis-to-sis: class unstated (was fully-black-box), reverse-class fully-black-box, unless ffr:verification-gap-8 or ccw:verification-gap-isis-sis-parameters splits the page first (CCwiki quarantines the forward direction meanwhile). (5) rsa-to-fac-dlo24.md: its directions differ in model, which no class field can say (RSA ⇒ FAC is trivial in the standard model; FAC ⇒ RSA is DLO24's generic-ring theorem). The trivial direction is already recorded as red-rsa-to-fac-rsa78 (fac-to-rsa-rsa78.md), so re-record the DLO24 page as the implication `hypotheses: [fac]`, `conclusion: rsa`, `class: free`, `model: other`; it states a reversed theorem, so per the stability contract retire red-rsa-to-fac-dlo24 and take red-fac-to-rsa-dlo24, renaming the page fac-to-rsa-dlo24.md.
items.rationale: The two directions of an equivalence can be different theorems with different classes (ISIS ⇔ SIS: one direction is immediate, the other 'holds only under conditions on the column count and norm bound'). A consumer that chains equivalences cannot tell which direction `class` covers, so CCwiki keeps its own table of all 7 eligible equivalences. The field must be required, not optional: an absent optional field reads the same as a manifest from before the field existed. Retires CCwiki's curation entries `equivalences:red-cpa-security-to-cpa-security`, `equivalences:red-isis-inhomogeneous-sis-to-sis`, `equivalences:red-linear-secret-sharing-schemes-lsss-to-msp`, `equivalences:red-module-lwe-to-lwe-ls15`, `equivalences:red-module-lwe-to-ring-lwe-ls15`, `equivalences:red-rabin-ot-to-ot` and `equivalences:red-rsa-to-fac-dlo24`.

items.summary: Refuted assumptions (circular evasive LWE, SIDH, SSDDH) carry no machine-readable marker; add an optional refuted-by on objects and variants, per formulation (ffr:schema-convention-10 option B)
items.proposed_action: Add an optional `refuted-by`, a list of reference wikilinks. On an object page it marks the page's own object only, never its variants (CSIDH on the SIDH page stays unmarked); in a variant's mapping form it sits beside `anchor` and `formal`. A family in which only some formulations are false gets no marker on its host: private-coin evasive LWE stays unmarked. (1) scripts/generate-relations.mjs: for the page object `...(p.fm["refuted-by"] ? { refutedBy: [].concat(p.fm["refuted-by"]) } : {})`; for a variant `...(typeof v === "object" && v?.["refuted-by"] ? { refutedBy: [].concat(v["refuted-by"]) } : {})`; both omitted when empty, as `formal` is. (2) scripts/lint.mjs: add "refuted-by" to OPTIONAL_KEYS with an error unless the page is an object page; the variants loop (around line 536, which today checks only `anchor`) also checks a mapping's keys are `anchor`, `formal` and `refuted-by` only (no page uses the mapping form today, so this flags nothing); each refuted-by entry must resolve to a reference page, by the edge-source check without the `folklore` token. (3) Docs: docs/relations-json.md § objects; in schema/README.md § Refutations are attacks, not barriers, add '…and the refuted object or variant carries `refuted-by`, so a consumer deriving consequences can mark implications from it vacuous.' (4) Pages: learning-with-errors.md `circular-evasive-lwe: {anchor: "#circular-evasive-lwe", refuted-by: ["[[AMYY25 - Evasive LWE Attacks, Variants & Obfustopia|AMYY25]]"]}`; supersingular-isogeny-diffie-hellman.md top-level `refuted-by: ["[[CD22 - An efficient key recovery attack on SIDH|CD22]]"]` and `ssddh: {anchor: "#decisional-variant-ssddh", refuted-by: ["[[CD22 - An efficient key recovery attack on SIDH|CD22]]"]}`.
items.rationale: The wiki states these refutations in prose only (learning-with-errors.md § Evasive LWE counterexamples and § Circular evasive LWE; supersingular-isogeny-diffie-hellman.md's opening paragraph and § Known Results). A consumer deriving consequences needs to know that an implication from a false assumption is vacuous; CCwiki keeps a list of three for it. Option B per formulation, with no inheritance from a page to its variants, never over-claims for a family of which only some formulations are false. Retires CCwiki's curation entries `refuted:circular-evasive-lwe`, `refuted:sidh` and `refuted:ssddh`.

items.summary: The lint accepts `model` on a barrier page but relations.json drops it; emit it, standard by default, and set it on no-rom-to-ke-hmo-19
items.proposed_action: (1) scripts/generate-relations.mjs, in barriers.push after `class`: `model: p.fm.model ?? "standard",` (always emitted, as on reductions). (2) scripts/lint-edges.mjs: RATIONALE_FIELDS.barrier.model = "model". (3) schema/README.md § Which model to record: replace 'On a barrier, which has no `model` field, the model's node is the hypothesis' with '`model` on a barrier is the model its theorem is proved in, `standard` by default. A barrier saying X fails in a model also keeps the model's node as its hypothesis.' (4) content/Barriers/no-rom-to-ke-hmo-19.md: `model: rom`. content/Barriers/no-agm-to-ggm-kz22.md: as ffr:schema-convention-9 decides. No other barrier needs one today: the oracle separations are `relativizing`, not idealised-model theorems.
items.rationale: Without a model, a consumer propagating a primitive-to-primitive barrier through side reductions treats it as proved in the standard model; one proved only in an idealised model would be propagated wrongly. CCwiki reads the field the day it appears. Retires no CCwiki curation entry.

items.summary: Kil88's OT ⇒ MPC and OT ⇒ COM instantiate an ideal OT secure against malicious parties, but their hypothesis is the semi-honest ot node; re-point them at malicious-ot-security
items.proposed_action: (1) ot-to-mpc-kil88.md and ot-to-com.md: `hypotheses: [malicious-ot-security]` (the variant exists on oblivious-transfer.md#malicious-security). (2) cpir-to-ot-dmo00.md: `conclusion: malicious-ot-security`; its Statement already says non-trivial single-server PIR is complete for secure two-party and multi-party computation. (3) A new folklore page content/Reductions/malicious-ot-security-to-ot.md: `hypotheses: [malicious-ot-security]`, `conclusion: ot`, `class: fully-black-box`, `model: standard`, rationale.class 'The identity map: a protocol secure against malicious parties is secure against semi-honest ones.' Confirm this holds for the OT page's definitions. (4) oblivious-transfer.md § Malicious Security: define the variant as stand-alone, simulation-based security against a static malicious adversary, the notion Kil88's substitution of a real OT for the ideal one consumes; the section's game-based definitions, which it says 'do not capture all malicious-sender attacks', are not enough for it. Ids stay: this is node refinement on the same theorem.
items.rationale: ot-to-mpc-kil88.md's Statement computes every functionality 'with unconditional security against malicious parties' in the OT-hybrid model, and ot-to-com.md's binding relies on the committer not learning which bits arrived; both use an ideal OT. The ot node's definitions are semi-honest (oblivious-transfer.md § Malicious Security: 'The definitions above are **semi-honest**'), so chaining EGL's semi-honest OT into them proves more than the papers do. Checked by patching the manifest: every answer survives under the variant's name, and DDH ⇒* MPC still holds through DMO00. Retires CCwiki's curation entries `requires:red-ot-to-mpc-kil88:ot` and `requires:red-ot-to-com:ot`.

items.summary: GPSW06 concludes selective KP-ABE, PRP ⇒ iPRF only the forward-oracle game, and Kil88 with GMW87 only static malicious MPC with abort, but all three record the full node; conclude the variants instead
items.proposed_action: (1) bdh-to-abe-gpsw06.md: `conclusion: abe-selective-security` (the variant exists). (2) pseudorandom-function.md: under § Invertible PRFs, add a heading for the forward-oracle notion (the game Game^prf, without the inversion oracle) with the variant `invertible-prf-forward`. (3) prp-to-invertible-prf.md: `conclusion: invertible-prf-forward` (node refinement; the id stays). (4) Two new folklore pages, `class: fully-black-box`, `model: standard`: invertible-prf-to-invertible-prf-forward.md, `hypotheses: [invertible-prf]`, `conclusion: invertible-prf-forward` (the strong game implies the forward one), and invertible-prf-forward-to-prf.md, `hypotheses: [invertible-prf-forward]`, `conclusion: prf` (the forward game is the PRF game, as invertible-prfs-to-prf.md's Sketch says). (5) secure-multi-party-computation.md: add a heading for security with abort against a static malicious adversary corrupting any number of parties, stand-alone, with the variant `mpc-security-with-abort`; ot-to-mpc-kil88.md: `conclusion: mpc-security-with-abort` (node refinement; the id stays).
items.rationale: bdh-to-abe-gpsw06.md's Statement gives a key-policy ABE that is 'selectively KP-IND-CPA-secure', and the ABE page says 'Selective security is strictly weaker than adaptive security'. prp-to-invertible-prf.md's Statement gives an invertible PRF 'for the traditional (forward-oracle) game', and says strong security 'fails for every permutation'. Recording the full nodes lets a consumer chain a selective scheme into an adaptive construction (ABE ⇒ IBE). The patched manifest keeps each pair under the variant's name. ot-to-mpc-kil88.md's Statement gives GMW87's n-party protocol 'with security with abort against a malicious dishonest majority', while the MPC page's malicious notion is 'typically with guaranteed output delivery or fairness conditions' and the page also covers UC security; Kil88 and GMW87 give no fairness, guaranteed output delivery, adaptive or UC security (the maintainer's PR #9 audit). Nothing consumes MPC, so no pair is lost. Retires CCwiki's curation entries `weakens:red-bdh-to-abe-gpsw06`, `weakens:red-prp-to-invertible-prf` and `weakens:red-ot-to-mpc-kil88`.

items.summary: Sixteen hypotheses need a hardness regime, group, field or domain size their node does not define; re-point each at a variant that states it (YZW+19's and AMR25's are already proposed by ffr:node-granularity-3 and -11)
items.proposed_action: Re-point each hypothesis at a variant that states the notion its Statement needs; ids stay (node refinement). (1) dlog-to-prg-bm84.md: `dlog` → new `dlog-zp-star`, a heading 'DLOG in $\ZZ_p^*$' on discrete-logarithm.md. (2) tdp-to-nizk-bfm88.md: `tdp` → new `doubly-enhanced-certified-tdp` on trapdoor-permutation.md, beside enhanced-trapdoor-permutation. (3) pke-to-com.md: `pke` → a new variant for perfectly correct CPA-secure PKE with certifiable keys on public-key-encryption.md. (4) abe-to-be.md: `abe` → the existing `cp-abe-adaptive-security`; set KW19's (k-linear-assumption-to-abe-rw13.md) and Wee25's (succinct-lwe-to-abe-wee25.md) conclusions likewise if their Statements are adaptive CP-ABE (needs the papers). (5) subexponential-lpn-to-ot-yz16.md, subexponential-lpn-to-pke-yz16.md, subexponential-lpn-to-prc-cg24.md and lwe-to-zero-bit-prc-cg24.md: `subexponential-lpn` → one new variant on learning-parity-with-noise.md for constant-noise LPN that is $2^{\omega(\sqrt{n})}$-hard, if YZ16's and CG24's regimes agree (needs the papers), plus a folklore edge to it from the above-half variant of ffr:node-granularity-3. (6) lwe-to-leveled-fully-homomorphic-encryption-bgv12.md: `lwe` → a new LWE variant on learning-with-errors.md with modulus-to-noise ratio exponential in the depth, which Pei09 concludes (ccw:missing-edge-lwe-classical). (7) fe-to-io.md: `functional-encryption` → a new variant on functional-encryption.md for single-key, sub-exponentially secure, weakly compact public-key FE. (8) ddh-and-lpn-and-lwe-and-nc1-prg-to-io-jls21.md: `sxdh`, `lwe`, `lpn`, `prg-in-nc0` → sub-exponential variants of each (on decisional-diffie-hellman.md, learning-with-errors.md, learning-parity-with-noise.md and low-complexity-prg.md), with LPN over $\ZZ_p$; the shared prime $p$ stays in the Statement. YZW+19 and AMR25 are not repeated here: ffr:node-granularity-3 and ffr:node-granularity-11 already propose their variants. (9) prp-to-prf.md and prp-to-invertible-prf.md: `prp` → new `prp-large-domain` on pseudorandom-permutation.md, a PRP over a domain with $|\calD| = \secpar^{\omega(1)}$; prf-to-prp-lr88.md concludes it (its PRP is on $\bits^{2n}$, and its bound is negligible only when $2^n$ is superpolynomial); strong-security-to-prp.md keeps the plain node; a new folklore page prp-large-domain-to-prp.md, the identity, keeps every other use. Both conversions need it: with only one re-pointed, the other bypasses it. LR88's own hypothesis has the same gap one step back: its PRP is large-domain only under its premise, a PRF on $\bits^n$ with $2^n$ superpolynomial (its Notes), and the prf node does not bound the domain (a PRF on a polynomial-size domain exists unconditionally, its key a whole random table); so when prf-to-prp-lr88.md concludes `prp-large-domain`, its hypothesis should be a new `prf-large-domain` on pseudorandom-function.md, with a folklore identity page prf-large-domain-to-prf.md, concluded by the PRF constructions whose Statements give a superpolynomial domain (needs the papers for which do). Not asked: Wat09's IBE and HIBE need DBDH and DLIN in one group, which no node can say. GPSW06's DBDH is ccw:node-dbdh.
items.rationale: Each of these Statements needs more of its hypothesis than the node defines, so a chain into it from an edge that concludes only the node proves more than the paper does: BM84's 'If DLOG is hard in $\ZZ_p^*$' is fed DLOG in CDH's or BDH's group (32 derived pairs on wiki ab81f02); FLS90 needs 'doubly enhanced, certified' permutations; BGV12 a modulus-to-noise ratio exponential in $L$, where Reg05 gives a prime $\poly(n)$ modulus; AJ15/BV15 'single-key, sub-exponentially secure and weakly compact' FE; PRP ⇒ PRF and PRP ⇒ iPRF 'a domain $\calD$ with $|\calD|$ superpolynomial in $\secpar$', which the PRP page's syntax does not bound (on $\calD = \{0,1\}$, $P_k(x) = x \oplus k$ for a uniform bit $k$ is a perfect PRP and not a PRF: two queries never collide, while a random function's collide with probability 1/2). Variant nodes say this in the record, as ffr:node-granularity-3 and -11 do for LPN. Retires CCwiki's curation entries `requires:red-dlog-to-prg-bm84:dlog`, `requires:red-tdp-to-nizk-bfm88:tdp`, `requires:red-pke-to-com:pke`, `requires:red-abe-to-be:abe`, `requires:red-subexponential-lpn-to-crhf-yzw-19:subexponential-lpn`, `requires:red-subexponential-lpn-to-ot-yz16:subexponential-lpn`, `requires:red-subexponential-lpn-to-pke-yz16:subexponential-lpn`, `requires:red-subexponential-lpn-to-prc-cg24:subexponential-lpn`, `requires:red-lwe-to-zero-bit-prc-cg24:subexponential-lpn`, `requires:red-noise-level-to-tdh-amr25:lpn-low-noise`, `requires:red-lwe-to-leveled-fully-homomorphic-encryption-bgv12:lwe`, `requires:red-fe-to-io:functional-encryption`, `requires:red-ddh-and-lpn-and-lwe-and-nc1-prg-to-io-jls21:sxdh`, `requires:red-ddh-and-lpn-and-lwe-and-nc1-prg-to-io-jls21:lpn` `requires:red-ddh-and-lpn-and-lwe-and-nc1-prg-to-io-jls21:prg-in-nc0`, `requires:red-prp-to-prf:prp` and `requires:red-prp-to-invertible-prf:prp`. CCwiki keeps one JLS21 entry, on the new LWE hypothesis, for the shared prime p.

items.summary: KEM + SKE ⇒ PKE needs only a one-time-secure SKE (the DEM), but its hypothesis is the whole ske node; add a one-time variant and re-point it
items.proposed_action: (1) symmetric-key-encryption.md: add the heading 'One-time security' with the variant `ske-one-time`. (2) kem-and-ske-to-pke.md: `hypotheses: [kem, ske-one-time]` (node refinement; the id stays). (3) Two new folklore pages: ske-to-ske-one-time.md, `hypotheses: [ske]`, `conclusion: ske-one-time`; and prg-to-ske-one-time.md, `hypotheses: [prg]`, `conclusion: ske-one-time` (a pseudorandom pad; encrypt-then-MAC with a one-time MAC for the CCA notion).
items.rationale: The Statement says 'a one-time-secure SKE (the DEM)', so the record asks for more than the theorem uses: KEM alone never gives PKE, and the 15 pairs that reach PKE through CS03 all need a second object for SKE. With ccw:missing-edge-owf's KEM ⇒ OWF, KEM would derive PKE. Retires no CCwiki curation entry.

items.summary: Ten folklore and textbook X ⇒ OWF results are not recorded (OT, SKE, COM, CRHF, MAC, PRF, SIS, LPN, KEM, one-time signatures); DLOG ⇒ OWF is ccw:missing-edge-dlog-to-owf
pages: content/References/BFKL93 - Cryptographic Primitives Based on Hard Learning Problems.md (new)
content/References/Hai08 - Semi-Honest to Malicious Oblivious Transfer The Black-Box Way.md (new)
items.proposed_action: Add ten reduction pages, each `conclusion: owf`, `model: standard`, the class as the source states it: {ot} ⇒ owf (semi-honest OT gives OWFs: Haitner, TCC 2008, Theorem 4, p. 425, per the maintainer's PR #9 audit; or IL89, find which theorem); {ske} ⇒ owf (IL89); {com} ⇒ owf (IL89); {crhf} ⇒ owf (folklore, for a compressing family); {mac} ⇒ owf (IL89); {prf} ⇒ owf (folklore); {sis} ⇒ owf (Ajt96); {lpn} ⇒ owf (folklore, or BFKL93, whose reference page is new); {kem} ⇒ owf (IL89 does not treat KEMs: find the source); {one-time-signature} ⇒ owf (Rom90). The reference pages for IL89, Ajt96 and Rom90 exist; Hai08's is new. DLOG ⇒ OWF, once in this list, is ccw:missing-edge-dlog-to-owf, with its exact formulation.
items.rationale: Each is a standard result the record lacks, so consumers of relations.json miss every consequence through OWF. Measured on wiki ab81f02 with CCwiki's curation after the PR #9 audit and R13's metBy change, by adding each alone as a standard-model folklore implication of unstated class: new derived pairs (of 999) are OT 169, SKE 93, COM 105, CRHF 47, MAC 48, PRF 33, SIS 16, LPN 31, KEM 17, one-time signatures 15; all ten together 372, and 404 with DLOG ⇒ OWF. (Before the audit: of 1,022, all eleven together 432.) Retires no CCwiki curation entry.

items.summary: Pei09's and BLPRS13's classical GapSVP ⇒ LWE reductions are cited in gapsvp-to-lwe-reg05's Notes but recorded as no edge, so every GapSVP chain is quantum
items.proposed_action: Add two reduction pages, both `hypotheses: [gapsvp]`, `model: standard`: gapsvp-to-lwe-pei09.md, concluding the LWE variant for large moduli that ccw:node-hypothesis-regimes proposes for BGV12 (Pei09, classical, $q \ge 2^{n/2}$); and gapsvp-to-lwe-blprs13.md, `conclusion: lwe` (BLPRS13, classical, with the dimension loss in security-loss). Check each regime in the papers.
items.rationale: gapsvp-to-lwe-reg05.md's Notes cite both (lines 32–33). With them GapSVP ⇒ PKE loses its quantum tag and, through BGV12 re-pointed at the same LWE variant, GapSVP ⇒ leveled FHE holds classically, which today's record cannot say. Retires no CCwiki curation entry.

items.summary: BDOZ11's MPC with preprocessing needs a large plaintext field, which its Statement does not say, so GM84's Z_2 encryption appears to feed it
items.proposed_action: Read BDOZ11 for the plaintext-space requirement of its semi-homomorphic encryption and state it in the Statement, cited. Then either re-point the hypothesis at a large-field variant of additively-homomorphic-encryption, or leave the hypothesis and let consumers read the condition from the Statement.
items.rationale: As recorded, QR ⇒ MPC with preprocessing follows through GM84's additively homomorphic encryption over $\ZZ_2$, which BDOZ11's protocol does not use. CCwiki adds no condition the wiki does not state, so the chain stands until the Statement says it. Retires no CCwiki curation entry.

items.summary: The bdh node defines computational BDH and DBDH together, but GPSW06 (and Wat09) assume decisional BDH; give DBDH its own variant, re-point them, and add DBDH ⇒ BDH
items.proposed_action: (1) bilinear-map-assumptions.md: make the Decisional BDH paragraph a heading with the variant `dbdh`, for the symmetric prime-order pairing groups the pages use. (2) bdh-to-abe-gpsw06.md: `hypotheses: [dbdh]` (node refinement; the id stays); likewise bdh-to-ibe-wat09.md and bdh-to-hibe-wat09.md, whose Statements say DBDH. (3) A new folklore page dbdh-to-bdh.md: `hypotheses: [dbdh]`, `conclusion: bdh`, `class: fully-black-box`, `model: standard`, rationale 'A BDH solver's output decides the DBDH challenge with one comparison, so DBDH hardness implies computational BDH hardness in the same group.'
items.rationale: bdh-to-abe-gpsw06.md's Statement begins 'If decisional bilinear Diffie–Hellman (DBDH) holds', and its Sketch embeds a DBDH challenge (g^a, g^b, g^c, Z) in the symmetric pairing e(g,g); GPSW06's group has prime order (GPSW06, §2 and §4.3, Theorem 1). The bdh node's page defines computational BDH and DBDH together, so a chain from computational BDH alone invokes GPSW06, though DBDH hardness implies computational BDH hardness; no converse is known (GPSW06 supplies none). Retires CCwiki's curation entry `requires:red-bdh-to-abe-gpsw06:bdh`.

items.summary: Selective KP-ABE gives CPA-secure PKE by a direct argument, but the record has no such edge, so BDH ⇒ PKE is not derived
items.proposed_action: A new page abe-selective-security-to-pke.md: `hypotheses: [abe-selective-security]` (which GPSW06 concludes with ccw:node-weakened-conclusions), `conclusion: pke`, `class: fully-black-box`, `model: standard`, source folklore. Construction: fix an attribute set $x_0$ and a policy $f_0$ with $f_0(x_0) = 1$; key generation runs the ABE's $\Setup$, publishes its public parameters as the public key and keeps $\KeyGen(\msk, f_0)$ as the secret key; every message is encrypted under $x_0$ and decrypted with the key for $f_0$; correctness is the ABE's. Reduction: a PKE adversary becomes a selective KP-ABE adversary that commits to $x_0$ before $\Setup$, makes no key query, and forwards the PKE challenge messages; the distinguishing advantage is preserved. State that the analogous identity encoding of a selective KP-ABE gives selective IBE, not adaptive IBE. Link it from attribute-based-encryption.md § Selective Security.
items.rationale: GPSW06 gives selectively KP-IND-CPA-secure KP-ABE (GPSW06, §2 and §4.3, Theorem 1); the argument above runs against that selective game and is not a theorem attributed to GPSW06. Measured on wiki ab81f02 with GPSW06 concluding abe-selective-security: +41 derived pairs (999 → 1,040), BDH ⇒ PKE among them (assuming DBDH, until ccw:node-dbdh); BDH ⇒ IBE and BDH ⇒ BE stay underived, as they should. From the maintainer's PR #9 audit. Retires no CCwiki curation entry.

items.summary: DLOG ⇒ OWF on the same cyclic group family is not recorded, so CDH ⇒ PRG is not derived: BM84 needs DLOG in Z_p^*, not in CDH's group
items.proposed_action: A new page dlog-to-owf.md: `hypotheses: [dlog]`, `conclusion: owf`, `class: fully-black-box`, `model: standard`, folklore. Statement: for an efficiently generated and efficiently represented cyclic group family of known order $q$ with generator $g$ on which DLOG is hard, $x \mapsto g^x$ on $\ZZ_q$ is one-way; an inverter given $g^x$ returns some $x'$ with $g^{x'} = g^x$, so $x' \equiv x \pmod q$, the discrete logarithm. State it in the public-parameter formulation: the function's index is the group description $(\GG, q, g)$ the group generator samples, the domain sample is a uniform $x \in \ZZ_q$, and one-wayness is over both. It uses no integer reading of group elements and is not BM84's. List it in discrete-logarithm.md's Known Results.
items.rationale: BM84's construction reads residues of $\ZZ_p^*$ as integers (ccw:content-bm84-rationale), so DLOG in CDH's, DDH's or BDH's own group does not instantiate it, and CCwiki refuses it there. The general existence implication does not need BM84: with DLOG ⇒ OWF and the recorded OWF ⇒ PRG (HILL99, Theorem 6.2.2, manuscript p. 33), CDH ⇒ PRG follows fully black-box. Measured on wiki ab81f02: +32 derived pairs (999 → 1,031), CDH ⇒ PRG and BDH ⇒ PRG among them. DDH ⇒ PRG already holds through ElGamal, IL89 and HILL99. Sources: BM84, §§3–4, Theorem 4 (pp. 861–862). From the maintainer's PR #9 audit. Retires no CCwiki curation entry.

items.summary: Haitner's fully black-box compiler from semi-honest to malicious OT is not recorded, so semi-honest OT never reaches Kil88's OT ⇒ MPC and OT ⇒ COM; record it, and state what Kil88, DMO00 and OT ⇒ COM conclude
pages: content/References/Hai08 - Semi-Honest to Malicious Oblivious Transfer The Black-Box Way.md (new)
items.proposed_action: (1) A new page ot-to-malicious-ot-security-hai08.md: `hypotheses: [ot]`, `conclusion: malicious-ot-security` (the variant exists on oblivious-transfer.md#malicious-security), `class: fully-black-box`, `model: standard`, source Hai08 (Haitner, TCC 2008; its reference page is new): Theorem 2 and Corollary 2 (p. 415); no separate OWF assumption, since semi-honest OT gives OWFs (Theorem 4, p. 425). The Statement says which malicious security the compiled OT has: stand-alone, simulation-based security against a static malicious adversary, the notion Kil88's substitution of a real OT for the ideal one consumes, and so the notion ccw:node-malicious-ot's `malicious-ot-security` should be defined by on oblivious-transfer.md, not the page's game-based malicious definitions, which it says 'do not capture all malicious-sender attacks'. Confirm the notion against Hai08's definitions, Theorem 2 and Corollary 2. (2) With ccw:node-malicious-ot, Kil88's two pages take `malicious-ot-security`, and the chain is the compiler then the direct Kil88 step; without it, extend both Statements and their citations to include the compiler. (3) ot-to-mpc-kil88.md: conclude explicitly static malicious MPC with abort (ccw:node-weakened-conclusions' `mpc-security-with-abort`); no fairness, guaranteed output delivery, adaptive or UC security is inherited. (4) cpir-to-ot-dmo00.md: record the malicious upgrade its completeness claim rests on (the OT its PIR gives, made secure against malicious parties by a semi-honest-to-malicious compiler). (5) ot-to-com.md: say the commitment is statistically hiding and statistically binding in the OT-hybrid model only; with a real OT its hiding and binding rest on that OT's security, and no plain-model commitment is both statistically hiding and statistically binding.
items.rationale: Kil88's two Statements substitute a real OT for an ideal one, which needs OT secure against malicious parties, while the OT page's definitions are semi-honest; CCwiki therefore refuses them on semi-honest OT, and ETDP ⇒ MPC and ETDP ⇒ COM are not derived. Measured on wiki ab81f02, the compiler with ccw:node-malicious-ot's re-pointing (its two requirements dropped) gives 32 new full derived pairs (999 → 1,031): 23 X ⇒ malicious OT, 6 X ⇒ COM (ETDP ⇒ COM among them), and malicious OT ⇒ OT, Rabin OT and OIHF; and 6 weakened-only X ⇒ MPC pairs, ETDP ⇒ MPC among them as static malicious MPC with abort (Kil88's conclusion); ccw:node-malicious-ot alone adds 20 full pairs net and leaves ETDP ⇒ MPC underived. From the maintainer's PR #9 audit. Retires no CCwiki curation entry by itself.

items.summary: Only the ciphertext-policy ABE ⇒ BE construction is recorded; adaptive KP-ABE with membership policies gives adaptive BE too
items.proposed_action: A new page kp-abe-to-be.md (or a second construction with its own edge beside abe-to-be.md, which keeps the CP construction): from an adaptively KP-IND-CPA-secure KP-ABE over attribute universe $[n]$ whose policy class contains the membership predicates $f_i(x) = [i \in x]$, to `be`; `class: fully-black-box`, `model: standard`, folklore. User $i$ gets the KP-ABE key for $f_i$; a broadcast to $S \subseteq [n]$ encrypts under the attribute set $S$, so user $i$ decrypts exactly when $i \in S$. The forbidden BE key queries (users $i \in S^*$) are exactly the policies $f_i$ that accept $S^*$, so every BE adversary is a KP-ABE adversary with the same advantage and the security game is preserved. State that selective KP-ABE gives only selective BE, and that neither construction gives short ciphertexts.
items.rationale: abe-to-be.md's Statement takes a CP-ABE whose policy class contains disjunctions, so a consumer cannot reach BE from KP-ABE. With it, ABE ⇒ BE needs either CP-ABE with disjunctions or adaptive KP-ABE with membership policies: the KP route carries its own condition, which CCwiki would enforce with a requirement citing the new Statement unless the edge's hypothesis is a variant that states it. Measured on wiki ab81f02 with the KP edge taking the plain abe node and no such requirement: 1 new derived pair (circular evasive LWE ⇒ BE, vacuous); GPSW06's selective KP-ABE still reaches no BE, since the record has no selective-BE node. From the maintainer's PR #9 audit. Retires no CCwiki curation entry.

items.summary: dlog-to-prg-bm84.md's rationale says the construction 'uses only the group operation', but it reads residues of Z_p^* as integers
items.proposed_action: Rewrite `rationale.class`: the construction uses the group operation of $\ZZ_p^*$ and the integer reading of residues, as the next exponent in $x_{i+1} = g^{x_i} \bmod p$ and in the half-interval predicate $[x_i \ge (p-1)/2]$; the reduction runs the distinguisher only as an oracle, turning it into a next-bit predictor and the predictor into a DLOG solver.
items.rationale: The recurrence feeds each residue back as an integer exponent and the output bit compares residues by their integer order: an interface of the prime field $\ZZ_p$ that an arbitrary cyclic group's encoding does not supply. This is why BM84 needs DLOG in $\ZZ_p^*$ (BM84, §§3–4, Theorem 4, pp. 861–862), and why DLOG in another group does not instantiate it; the general DLOG ⇒ PRG implication goes through ccw:missing-edge-dlog-to-owf instead. From the maintainer's PR #9 audit. Retires no CCwiki curation entry; ccw:node-hypothesis-regimes' `dlog-zp-star` row retires `requires:red-dlog-to-prg-bm84:dlog`.

items.summary: rsa-to-fac-dlo24.md lets the preprocessing see the eventual modulus n, which would make factoring trivial; DLO24 fixes the advice before the modulus is sampled, and its model is not only ring operations
items.proposed_action: (1) Restate the experiment from DLO24's Definitions 15–16 (p. 8:18) and Definition 28 (p. 8:23), and the theorem from Theorem 12 (p. 8:15): a generic-RSA adversary with preprocessing, whose advice is computed from the security parameter and the random encoding before the modulus and challenge are sampled, converts into a factoring adversary with preprocessing of the same kind, with polynomially related online complexity and polynomially longer advice; say the model permits a non-generic intermediate computation on the encoded challenge, instead of 'only through ring operations and equality tests'. (2) Keep the ordinary direction separate: RSA hardness implies factoring hardness on the same modulus distribution, fully black-box in the standard model, which fac-to-rsa-rsa78.md (`red-rsa-to-fac-rsa78`) records. With ccw:schema-reverse-class's split, the page becomes FAC ⇒ RSA, `model: other`, its hypothesis a new variant on factoring.md for factoring hardness against adversaries with preprocessing advice fixed before $N$ is sampled (the fac node's adversary gets no advice); its `free` class holds inside the generic-RSA experiment only.
items.rationale: The Statement says the adversary may receive 'an advice string from unbounded preprocessing on $n$'. Preprocessing that saw $N = pq$ could put $p$ in its polynomial-length advice and factor online trivially, so that cannot be the theorem. CCwiki keeps the reverse direction conditional on the corrected experiment. From the maintainer's PR #9 audit, which cites DLO24 (ITC 2024, LIPIcs 304, paper 8). Retires CCwiki's curation entry `requires:red-rsa-to-fac-dlo24~reverse:fac`, with ccw:schema-reverse-class's split.

items.summary: bdh-to-hve-bw07.md lists three joint assumptions, but BW07 needs two on one composite-order group family (cBDH and C3DH; subgroup decision follows from C3DH), and BW07's reference page has the wrong title
pages: content/References/BW07 - Conjunctive Normal Form Encryption and Attribute Based Encryption.md
items.proposed_action: (1) Restate the Statement: in a composite-order bilinear group family, HVE with selective payload- and attribute-hiding security exists under composite-order cBDH and C3DH on that same family (BW07, Definitions 4.1–4.2; Lemmas 5.3–5.6, pp. 11–12); the bilinear subgroup decision assumption follows from C3DH (Appendix B.2 and footnote 2, p. 21: relabel the subgroups and apply the pairing). (2) Rename the reference page to 'BW07 - Conjunctive, Subset, and Range Queries on Encrypted Data.md' (its heading already has this title) and update the links in bdh-to-hve-bw07.md and hve-to-subset-and-range-queries.md. (3) Record the two hypotheses as nodes on that one family, as fu2:node-granularity-13 proposes, rather than the prime-order bdh.

items.summary: isis-inhomogeneous-sis-to-sis.md proves SIS ⇒ ISIS but says only that ISIS ⇒ SIS 'holds only under conditions on the column count and norm bound'; state the parameters, distributions and a proof, or split the page
items.proposed_action: Either state ISIS hardness ⇒ SIS hardness with explicit parameter inequalities, the instance distributions and a proof or reference; or split the page into the implication SIS ⇒ ISIS (SIS hard for $(n, m, q, \sqrt{\beta^2+1})$ ⇒ ISIS hard for $(n, m-1, q, \beta)$, the Sketch's fully black-box reduction: write $\mathbf{A} = [\mathbf{A}' \mid \mathbf{a}]$ and turn $\mathbf{A}'\mathbf{z}' = \mathbf{a}$ into the nonzero kernel vector $(\mathbf{z}', -1)$), and record the other direction only once it is stated.
items.rationale: 'The parameter regime where the implication holds' is circular, and read at fixed parameters the claim is false: with $q = 2$, $m = 1$, $n = \secpar$, $\beta = 2$, SIS is solved by $z = 2$, while a uniform ISIS target lies in the span of the single column with probability at most $2^{1-n}$. That counterexample is to an unrestricted fixed-parameter claim, not to a correctly parameterized equivalence. CCwiki quarantines the direction meanwhile. From the maintainer's PR #9 audit. Retires CCwiki's curation entry `quarantine:red-isis-inhomogeneous-sis-to-sis`.
